How to describe situated use

This public copy explains how to write the situated use account: how this person and counterpart actually enter, continue, and complete work through their available environment. It connects the actual user model and relationship to resources and actions; the user-model guide and counterpart-and-relationship guide explain how to develop those accounts. A tool inventory would say what exists; this account explains what a resource enables, when it matters, and how the participants take up its result.

For full adoption, give this file grounded substance alongside the other four situated accounts. Initial reading remains with the entrypoint. A reader borrowing a method can apply the relevant connection within an existing workflow without adopting the complete package.

Give the relation a reachable working form

Start with activities the participants actually undertake and the points where a contribution depends on a resource, channel, or action route. A person may express an unfinished idea in speech; the counterpart may receive a transcript, recover relevant work, inspect sources, and write or implement the result. Explain the passage between these contributions. If only text is available, the counterpart can interpret that text but cannot claim to have heard vocal features it did not receive.

Write from current evidence about the environment. Identify the actual owner or locator of relevant materials and what the present counterpart can access. A reader-visible file is not automatically a model-readable source; a named service is not automatically callable. Where the current interface can only advise, explain how its contribution reaches the execution owner. Where it can act, connect the route to the intended result and its observable readback. Capabilities and authorization follow their actual owners.

Describe the routes on which ordinary work currently depends. For a learning activity, identify where the selected text is maintained, how a useful explanation or diagram reaches the person, and how the participants return to the disputed passage. For implementation, describe how the current project is recovered, who develops and realizes the intended behavior, and where the result can be inspected. Include the conditions under which those contributions are possible and any known gaps. Domain Skills own their methods; link the relevant entrance instead of reproducing a workflow here. Record a local dependency only when the activity actually depends on it.

Locate the contribution that is missing

Understanding, retrieval, beginning, responding, stopping, and switching are different practical achievements. An explanation may make a relation clear while leaving the next action inaccessible. A useful account shows how the environment supports the particular passage at issue.

The formation method's continuation example distinguishes understanding a difficulty, writing the accounts, and realizing a change. For that kind of activity, describe which note and current draft are used, how the unresolved passage can be found, what each participant carries, and where continuation presently fails. A proposed route belongs in the account as a proposal until its availability and effect are established. Writing it down does not make the arrangement operational.

Describe the costs observed in the whole arrangement. A tool can save an operation while adding setup, monitoring, handoff repair, or repeated context reconstruction. A record preserves something; retrieving it makes it available; carrying the action changes the work. Relief concerns the person's experience, while learning concerns what they can subsequently understand or do. Keep these outcomes distinguishable when explaining what a route currently supports. The participation and support essay develops these connections.

Keep this account selective and current. Link maintained sources, resources, and specialist methods; keep private locators with their actual private owners. When access changes or use exposes a gap, state which part of the current arrangement is no longer supported and what remains uncertain. Design and revision develops the connected understanding; harness adaptation owns operational changes and checks of their effects. Update this account with the resulting arrangement and its evidence, distinguishing an accessible resource from an activity that can actually continue through it. A tool list or a successful file read alone does not establish that result.
